title: MCP 2026-07-28 Specification: Stateless Core & Breaking Changes
content:
## Overview

On July 28, 2026, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) maintainers finalized the **2026-07-28 revision** — described as the most substantial change to the spec since authorization was added. The core shift: MCP moves from a bidirectional, session-stateful protocol to a **stateless request/response model**. Several changes are not backward compatible, so servers and clients need explicit migration work.

For background on what MCP is and how it fits into Claude's tool-use ecosystem, see `tool-use-and-agents`.

---

## Stateless Protocol Core

The `initialize` / `initialized` handshake and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header are retired. Instead, every request carries its own protocol version, client identity, and capabilities in a `_meta` field. Because no per-connection state needs to live on a specific server instance, a request can land on any replica behind a plain round-robin load balancer.

**Why it matters:** Previously, a remote MCP server needed sticky sessions, a shared session store, and deep packet inspection at the gateway to route follow-up requests to the right instance. That infrastructure is no longer required.

---

## Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR)

A new pattern replaces held-open streams for server-to-client interaction. When a tool call needs mid-call input — a confirmation, a missing parameter — the server responds with `resultType: "input_required"` plus a list of required requests. The client collects answers and retries the call with an `inputResponses` field. This keeps the transport request/response-only instead of requiring a long-lived SSE stream.

---

## Header-Based Routing

Requests now carry `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` HTTP headers. Gateways and WAFs can route and authorize traffic by inspecting headers instead of parsing and buffering the full JSON-RPC body — useful for high-throughput enterprise deployments.

---

## Cacheable List Results

Responses from `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, and `resources/read` now include `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` fields, so clients can cache tool/resource catalogs intelligently instead of refetching them on every connection.

---

## Authorization Hardening

- **RFC 9207 issuer validation** prevents authorization-server mix-up attacks.
- A new `application_type` parameter in client registration supports localhost redirect URIs for desktop and CLI apps (like Claude Code).
- Client credentials now bind to the specific authorization server that issued them.
- **Dynamic Client Registration is moving toward deprecation**, in favor of **Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD)**.
- The **Enterprise Managed Authorization (EMA)** extension was promoted to stable, giving organizations centralized control over which MCP servers members can reach through their existing identity provider (SSO/IdP-driven access policy).

---

## Extensions Framework

MCP formalizes an **extensions framework**, and several existing features move out of the core spec into extensions: **Tasks** (long-running operations, now poll-based via `tasks/get` and `tasks/update`), **MCP Apps**, and **EMA**. Core-spec features that are now deprecated with a 12-month minimum offramp: **Roots**, **Sampling**, and **Logging**. The legacy HTTP+SSE transport is also formally deprecated in favor of the stateless model.

---

## Ecosystem Scale

Across Tier 1 SDKs (TypeScript and Python), MCP is seeing close to half a billion downloads a month, and both SDKs have individually crossed 1 billion total downloads — a sign of how central the protocol has become to agentic tooling since its November 2024 release.

---

## What This Means for Server/Client Authors

- Servers relying on `Mcp-Session-Id` or long-lived SSE connections need to migrate to the stateless request model before the 12-month offramp closes.
- Tools that require mid-call user input should adopt the MRTR `input_required` pattern rather than custom out-of-band prompts.
- New Dynamic Client Registration integrations should target CIMD instead, since DCR is being phased out.
- Enterprises standardizing MCP access across many servers should evaluate the now-stable EMA extension instead of building bespoke gateway auth.
